description:
pkix-lint/src/oscal/emit.rs's `finding_seed` (lines 776-793) and `risk_seed` (lines 797-807) build UUID v8 seed bytes by concatenating variable-length byte fields with only single-byte 0x00 separators:

```rust
fn finding_seed(report_seed: &[u8], i: usize, f: &Finding) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut buf = ...;
    buf.extend_from_slice(report_seed);
    buf.extend_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
    buf.extend_from_slice(f.lint_id.as_bytes());   // variable length, no length prefix
    buf.push(0);                                   // separator
    buf.push(severity_label[0]);
    if let Some(d) = result_detail(&f.result) {
        buf.extend_from_slice(d.as_bytes());       // variable length, no length prefix, no trailing separator
    }
    ...
}
```

`risk_seed` has the same pattern with `lint_id` and `deviation_id`.

Section G (algorithm and parameter choice — seed canonicalization). What goes wrong: integrity. Two distinct logical Findings or Deviations can be constructed to produce the same UUID v8 if the variable-length fields can carry a 0x00 byte.

Concrete construction:
- Finding A: `lint_id = "a"`, severity = w, detail = "X"
- Finding B: `lint_id = "a\x00wX"`, severity = ?, detail = ...

The discriminator "0x00 || severity_byte" written by A becomes part of B's lint_id when B claims a longer lint_id. Whether a *natural* collision exists depends on which severity_label byte values can appear in attacker-supplied lint_ids; the structural defect is the absence of length prefixing or canonical encoding.

`lint_id` is `Cow<'static, str>` populated either from static literals (safe) or from deserialized JSON (attacker-controlled). `Finding` derives Deserialize behind the `serde` feature, so a JSON Finding can carry arbitrary bytes including 0x00 in `lint_id`.

Practical impact: low. UUIDs are audit identifiers, not access tokens. Two Findings sharing a UUID v8 in OSCAL output causes observation/finding key collision in downstream tooling — a confusing audit trail, not a security boundary breach. Hence P3 rather than P1.

Defense-in-depth fix:
- Length-prefix every variable-length field (write `len.to_le_bytes()` before `as_bytes()`)
- Or hash a canonical serialization (CBOR/postcard) of the (i, lint_id, severity, detail, cert_index, cert_sha256) tuple

`EvidenceKey::seed` (lines 228-246) already does this correctly using tag bytes for Option discriminators. The fix is to apply the same discipline to finding_seed and risk_seed.

Note: `uuid_v8(NS, seed)` itself (lines 733-753) computes `SHA-256(namespace || 0x00 || seed)`. `namespace` is always a static literal containing no 0x00, so the namespace/seed boundary is safe; the defect is purely within the seed-construction helpers.
notes: Duplicate of PKIX-hy2e.41 (open, P3) filed in the prior crypto-security pass on pkix-lint. Same finding shape: finding_seed and risk_seed in oscal/emit.rs concatenate variable-length fields with single-byte separators rather than length-prefixing. hy2e.41 captured this 8 days ago; my pass independently identified it confirming the structural issue persists. Closing this issue as duplicate; the live tracking lives at PKIX-hy2e.41.
title: UUID v8 seed construction concatenates variable-length attacker-controllable fields without length prefixes
